title: Freya and the Orbit
premise: Dominic Whitlock, a clone decanted to inherit her original's unsolved murder investigation, arrives at Meridian Colony expecting a routine audit and finds a settlement quietly starving while Earth's fleet pretends it still exists. When the name 'Freya Voss' appears on the manifest of a ship that never launched, Dominic uncovers a decades-old conspiracy: half the colony's cryosleep berths were sold to fleet elites, dooming the other half to a slow death. As the truce between colony factions nears expiry, Dominic must choose between exposing the truth—which will ignite civil war—and preserving the fragile loyalty that keeps survivors alive, all while falling for Freya's daughter, who guards her mother's secret. In the end, Dominic broadcasts the manifest but brokers a shared awakening sequence, sacrificing her own berth and her original's legacy of silence so that both halves of humanity wake together.
about_author: Lena Winterbourne is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical reports about ships that never flew before turning to fiction. She lives in Reykjavik, where the long winters taught her that survival stories are really love stories in disguise.

chapters.title: The Inheritance of Dead Men
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Dominic wakes aboard the transport Halcyon, reviewing her original's murder file—a case closed by convenience, not evidence. She rehearses being him: his gait, his silences. The emotional beat is quiet dread; she is a copy arriving to solve a crime committed against the person she was made from.

chapters.title: Meridian, Population Declining
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. She lands at Meridian Colony and finds rusted greenhouses, ration queues, and officials reciting optimistic numbers that match no census she can find. Administrator Cole welcomes her with rehearsed warmth. The beat is creeping unease—the colony isn't hiding a murderer; it's hiding something larger.

chapters.title: A Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. In the archive vault, Dominic cross-references launch records and finds the freighter Perihelion listed as departed—yet its fuel logs show it never left pad nine. On its manifest: Freya Voss, a name absent from every living registry. The beat is the first true hook of obsession.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Daughter
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. She tracks the name to Sable Voss, the colony's reclusive archivist, who slams the door on questions about her mother. But Sable slips a data chip into Dominic's coat—unprompted, unexplained. The beat is reluctant connection; two women circling the same wound from opposite sides.

chapters.title: What the Ice Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sable's perspective reveals the chip contains her mother's final recordings: Freya discovered the fleet had sold half of Meridian's cryosleep berths to off-world elites. Sable has protected this secret for twenty years. The beat is the weight of inherited silence and love that looks like betrayal.

chapters.title: Rations and Rumors
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Dominic walks the lower terraces where colonists are dying slowly—malnutrition dressed up as 'transition protocols.' An old engineer, Ilya, hints he helped load the Perihelion with people, not cargo. The beat is moral vertigo: everyone knows, and no one says.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sable attends the faction council where North Terrace and Dockside leaders renew their armed ceasefire—expiring in ninety days. She realizes Dominic's investigation could shatter it. The beat is fear sharpening into resolve: some truths kill faster than lies.

chapters.title: Interrogating a Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Dominic confronts Administrator Cole with the Perihelion discrepancy; he counters by revealing he knows exactly what she is—a clone, legally property, her testimony worthless in fleet court. The beat is humiliation weaponized, and the first flicker of anger replacing duty.

chapters.title: Freya's Voice
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Listening to her mother's last recording together, Dominic and Sable hear Freya describe the berth auction—and her choice to stay behind so Sable could sleep. Sable confesses she woke early, trading her own berth back. The beat is grief becoming intimacy; the love line ignites.

chapters.title: Ilya's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Ilya admits he loaded forty-one people onto the Perihelion, which launched empty and burned up over the ice—they were executed to keep the berth sale quiet, including Dominic's original's key witness. Her murder case and the conspiracy fuse into one. The beat is horror clicking into purpose.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Loyalty
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sable begs Dominic to bury the evidence until after the truce renewal; Dominic refuses—her original died chasing this. Their first real fight. The beat is the central theme made flesh: loyalty to each other versus loyalty to the dead and the dying.

chapters.title: The Audit
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Fleet inspectors arrive unexpectedly; Cole stages a Potemkin colony tour. Dominic realizes the fleet isn't ignorant—it's complicit, auditing not conditions but leaks. The beat is isolation deepening: there is no outside authority coming to save anyone.

chapters.title: Night on Pad Nine
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sable takes Dominic to the scorched launch pad where the Perihelion fell; among the debris they find a child's shoe and an intact black box. The beat is tender devastation—love declared quietly in a graveyard, sealed by shared witness.

chapters.title: Black Box
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The box holds cockpit audio: the pilot refusing orders, the sounds of the executions, and a fleet officer's voice giving them. Dominic now holds proof that would end careers—or start a war. The beat is terrible power and the loneliness of holding it.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Someone copies the black box files; suspicion falls on Sable, and Dockside militants kidnap her to force disclosure. Dominic must choose: trade the evidence for Sable's life. The beat is panic and clarity—truth has a price, and it just got personal.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Dominic trades the black box to the militants for Sable, knowing Cole's forces witnessed the handoff. Both factions now believe the other holds proof of genocide. The truce clock accelerates. The beat is sacrifice disguised as rescue, consequences cascading.

chapters.title: Ninety Hours
chapters.summary: POV Sable. With the truce expiring, both factions mobilize. Sable, freed, uses her archive access to broadcast Freya's full recordings colony-wide—not the militants' version, the whole truth, names and all. The beat is courage born of exhaustion; the point of no return.

chapters.title: Cole's Last Order
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Cole attempts to purge the archives and arrest the 'clone anomaly'; Dominic confronts him publicly with the fleet officer's voice from the black box, breaking his authority in front of both militias. The beat is the climax's first strike—truth wielded as a blade instead of a bomb.

chapters.title: The Waking Vote
chapters.summary: POV Sable. At a colony-wide assembly, Sable proposes the impossible: a unified awakening schedule splitting remaining berths equally, ratified by both factions. Violence nearly erupts until Ilya and others testify. The beat is hope fought for, not given—democracy at gunpoint.

chapters.title: Berth 117
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The math leaves one berth short. Dominic surrenders hers—she is a copy; her life feels spendable—but Sable refuses to accept it, arguing before the assembly that a clone's life counts double if she chooses to give it. The beat is the love-versus-duty theme resolved: Sable claims Dominic's life as worth saving.

chapters.title: Launch Window
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The fleet responds to the broadcast with a quarantine order; the colony must launch its distress beacon and unified manifest before the jamming grid closes. Dominic flies the relay mission through debris fields, broadcasting everything—berth sale, executions, the vote. The beat is exhilaration and terror; the truth finally airborne.

chapters.title: Both Halves Wake
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Months later, the fleet relents under public exposure; the first unified awakening begins. Sable stands at Dominic's cryoberth—her name added at the last second by unanimous vote—and reads Freya's final letter aloud as the lid seals. The beat is bittersweet peace: love outlasting duty, survival shared or not at all.
